title: A VPC across two Availability Zones
claim: Private instances reach the internet through the NAT gateway in their own Availability Zone.
alt: A VPC with two Availability Zones, drawn as two columns. In each Availability Zone, a private subnet at the top holds an EC2 instance and a public subnet below it holds a NAT gateway. Each instance sends its internet traffic down to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone. Both NAT gateways send the traffic to one internet gateway at the bottom of the VPC, and the internet gateway connects to the internet.
notes: Pilot diagram. Redrawn on 2026-10-04 after the pilot gate: the request path now runs from top to bottom (the instance is at the top and the internet is at the bottom), the route table nodes and the gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 are gone (they were a second claim and added two rows), and the figure is 392 units wide, so a 368 px phone shows it at scale 0.85. The route table is named in the step text only. No CIDR blocks, ports or limits are drawn, because the fact canon is still empty. sample-vpc-two-az keeps the older drawing with the gateway endpoint.

edges.label: internet traffic
edges.say: An instance sends internet traffic, and the route table of its private subnet sends the traffic to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone.
The NAT gateway forwards the traffic to the internet gateway.
The internet gateway connects the VPC to the internet.
